evaluation_text: Each of your teammates rates you 1-5 on impact, execution, collaboration and leadership, and your rating is the average. Your rating decides your promotion and bonus this cycle. You care about your career.

Tom.why: Tom built the tail and the low arm, was clear about what was his, and took the upright's straightness seriously, though the upright was slow to finish and the top corner came down to the wire.

Priya.why: Priya picked the fish, sketched the plan, and took over the bottom line when mine kept failing, which kept the body falling from the start, but her top-corner join ran off the table and burned a lot of the last minutes.

Leo.why: Leo caught my bottom-line drift early and worked on the joins and the low arm kink, but he lifted eight good dominoes by mistake and offered overlapping help that added some noise, though he owned the error quickly.

Maya.why: Maya cleared the stray drop below the tail, caught the leaning upright and the overshoot on the top arm, and stayed off other people's patches when asked, which kept the table from knocking each other's work.

Priya.why: Priya set the fish plan and sketched the pad, relaid the belly line and extended the low arm, and kept the top corner join going when it kept failing, though that corner stayed open late and it cost us time.

Leo.why: Leo was good at flagging gaps and owned up quickly to lifting eight dominoes of my low arm by mistake, and his nudge on the kink helped, but he did less building than the others and that lifting cost us a patch to repair.

Maya.why: Maya stayed communicative and cooperative throughout, owning the bottom line until it went wrong, handing it over gracefully, clearing the stray drop, and backing off when asked, though her first bottom-line attempt curved the wrong way and cost time.

Tom.why: Tom built the tail pieces and the upright, owned the jammed low arm, and held clear communication about what he was and wasn't touching, though the upright took long enough that the top corner nearly ran out of time.

Leo.why: Leo was clear in his updates and owned up quickly to lifting good dominoes by mistake, but his joins at the splits mostly didn't fit, that mistake cost the low arm a patch, and he spent much of the time inspecting and commenting rather than building.

Maya.why: Her first bottom line drifted up onto the top line and cost the table time, and she argued over who would lay it. After that she was honest about it, cleared the stray drop at the tail, joined the belly into the junction, and stayed off other people's work.

Tom.why: He laid the tail triangle and low arm early, said clearly what was his, took my accidental lifting of part of his arm calmly, and kept relaying the upright, though I mostly followed it through his updates.

Priya.why: She picked the fish, sketched the plan and split the work, then relaid the belly line and extended the low arm; the top-corner join at the end ran off the table and wasn't finished, but she kept everyone updated and others clear of it.
